goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.css.scss relative require './vendor/normalize' resolves to app/assets/stylesheets/vendor/normalize which doesn't exist, causing Sprockets compile failure and 500s on the embed page

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` with Sprockets directives `//= require ./vendor/normalize` and `//= require ./common/foundation/base`, but the diff does not show the repository’s existing `app/assets/stylesheets/vendor/normalize` (or lack thereof). Since we can’t verify from the diff that the referenced asset path does not exist, the claim of a guaranteed Sprockets compile failure/500s is not verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New Gemfile dependencies ruby-readability and simple-rss are not added to the primary Gemfile.lock, breaking bundle install/CI and causing LoadError on the default stack

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile` and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, but there is no corresponding update shown for the primary `Gemfile.lock`. If the default/CI stack uses `Gemfile.lock`, this would leave the lockfile out of sync with the Gemfile and can cause bundle/CI failures or missing-gem LoadErrors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb requires 'jobs/regular/process_post' instead of the correct job file for Jobs::PollFeed

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the header is `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, but the spec is for `Jobs::PollFeed` (defined in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This require does not load PollFeed and appears unrelated, so the spec may rely on autoloading or fail with an uninitialized constant depending on test setup. The correct require would be for the PollFeed job file (e.g. `jobs/scheduled/poll_feed`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS/Atom feed content is imported with zero sanitization on the polling path; TopicEmbed.import stores it and Post#cook renders it verbatim via raw post.cooked in the embed view, allowing malicious script HTML from a feed to execute inside the embed iframe served from the Discourse origin with access to session cookies

adjudication.rationale: The polling path imports feed HTML and explicitly bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed it takes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, and the embed view renders it as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Nothing in this diff sanitizes/filters the feed HTML (unlike `import_remote`, which restricts tags/attributes via ruby-readability), so malicious script markup from a feed would be stored and rendered in pages served from the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The readability whitelist on tags is only applied in TopicEmbed.import_remote (HTTP-fetch path); the feed polling path bypasses it entirely

adjudication.rationale: Verified: TopicEmbed.import_remote (HTTP fetch) runs Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: ...) to constrain HTML, but the feed polling path in Jobs::PollFeed builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` directly. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html, meaning feed HTML is not run through the readability whitelist (or other rendering/sanitization pipeline).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The loading view has no failure state: if TopicRetriever#retrieve returns without creating a topic, the browser reloads every 30 seconds forever and each reload re-enqueues another retrieve_topic job, with no max-retry, error message, or expiry

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it always does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) unconditionally reloads the page every 30s, which will hit `#best` again and enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job again. There is no exit condition, max attempts, or error messaging in the view/controller; and TopicRetriever can legitimately return without creating a topic (e.g., `fetch_http` returns if `embed_by_username` user is blank, or remote fetch/import fails), leading to an infinite reload loop with repeated job enqueues (even if actual retrieval is throttled in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No URL canonicalization between embed.js's discourseEmbedUrl and poll_feed's i.link (or i.id fallback), so trailing slash/http-vs-https/query string differences cause duplicate topics for the same article

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact string match on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (unique index) and checks existence via `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...)` in both `EmbedController#best`/`TopicRetriever` and `Jobs::PollFeed`/`TopicEmbed.import`. There is no normalization/canonicalization of URLs before these operations (e.g., `embed.js` passes `discourseEmbedUrl` verbatim; `poll_feed` uses `i.link` or `i.id`; `TopicEmbed.import` only regex-checks scheme). Therefore semantically identical URLs differing by trailing slash, http vs https, query params, etc. will be treated as distinct and can create duplicate topics/embeds for the same article.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed uses i.id as fallback link which can be a urn:uuid:-style Atom id that fails the ^https? check silently and drops the item

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the fallback `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` can assign a non-HTTP(S) Atom id (e.g., `urn:uuid:...`). That value is then passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which immediately `return`s unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Result: such feed items are silently skipped/dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: i.content is never checked for presence; for Atom feeds exposing only summary, CGI.unescapeHTML(nil.scrub) raises NoMethodError, and with retry: false and no rescue one malformed item aborts the entire poll run and all subsequent hourly runs with no logging
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `i.content` may be absent/nil in many feeds (e.g., Atom with only summary), and calling methods like `scrub` on it can raise an exception. The candidate doesn’t explicitly mention falling back to `description`, but it identifies the same underlying nil-dereference bug caused by assuming `content` is always present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: i.title is passed unchecked; with skip_validations: true in TopicEmbed.import a blank title yields a topic with a null title

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` passes `i.title` directly. In TopicEmbed.import, when creating a new topic/post it calls `PostCreator.new(..., title: title, ..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, which explicitly bypasses validations. The diff does not show whether the DB enforces non-null/non-empty topic titles or how PostCreator handles blank titles, so the specific claim that it will create a topic with a NULL title is not verifiable from the diff. However, the unchecked title combined with `skip_validations: true` is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/data-quality concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook raw_html early return bypasses Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) and the post analyzer, so plugin hooks (emoji, oneboxes, custom filters) are silently dropped for imported posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an early return in `Post#cook`: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips both `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. Imported posts created via `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and the new spec asserts `post.cooked.should == post.raw`, indicating this bypass is intentional. However, the finding is correct that plugin after-cook hooks (and analyzer-based transformations) will not run for these posts, which is a real, diff-grounded integration/architecture concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: word_count/reading_time stay nil for raw_html posts since no analyzer runs, breaking the migrate_word_counts invariant for new posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new cook_method enum and makes `Post#cook` return `raw` immediately when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), skipping `post_analyzer.cook(*args)`. New embedded/RSS-imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If word_count/reading_time are normally derived as part of the cooking/analyzer pipeline, these raw_html posts will not go through that path and can remain with derived fields unset (e.g., `word_count` staying NULL as referenced by the existing `MigrateWordCounts` migration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController assumes the found topic always exists and is viewable; a deleted topic makes TopicView.new raise RecordNotFound causing a 500 inside the embed iframe

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns an id, the code unconditionally does `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no existence/visibility check or rescue. If a `TopicEmbed` row exists but its associated topic has been deleted (or otherwise cannot be loaded), `TopicView.new` would typically try to load the topic by id and can raise (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`), producing a 500 inside the iframe. The diff introduces this path and does not handle it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb dereferences @topic_view.topic.url unconditionally in the header while the else branch links to the topic, so a topic with the first post deleted renders a header linking to a topic with zero posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb, both the if and else branches intentionally link to `@topic_view.topic.url`; the conditional only changes the link text (`embed.title` vs `embed.start_discussion`). There is no unconditional dereference that contradicts the else branch, and a topic having zero posts would still reasonably link to the topic URL. The diff does not show any scenario where `@topic_view.topic` would be nil when this template is rendered (controller renders `loading` when no `topic_id`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client locale adds an admin 'Embedding' tab label but the diff contains no admin route, template, or controller for that tab; the four new settings are only settable via console, so admins cannot configure embedding via UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `embedding:` section to `config/site_settings.yml` with four settings, and adds server-side i18n strings for those setting labels/descriptions in `config/locales/server.en.yml`. In Discourse, admin settings UI is generated from `site_settings.yml` categories/keys, so no dedicated admin route/controller/template is required for settings to be configurable via the UI. The added client locale string `embedding: "Embedding"` is consistent with adding a settings category label, not a missing tab implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The origin check in embed.js uses a substring test (indexOf) instead of origin equality, so origins like http://forum.example.com.attacker.com are accepted, allowing crafted discourse-resize messages from malicious pages
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: origin validation relies on indexOf/substring matching rather than strict origin equality, allowing attacker-controlled domains that contain the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com or forum.example.com.attacker.com) to bypass the check and send malicious messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task refactor removes category option and created_at timestamp, silently losing category import and original post dates, unrelated to PR intent

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the PR removes the `:category` option and the logic that looked up `category_id`, and it replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` create the post via `PostCreator.new(... title: title, raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` without passing `created_at` or `category`, so imported Disqus threads will no longer preserve original timestamps or allow setting a category via the task.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing migration create_top_topics.rb changed to force: true, which drops and recreates top_topics data on re-run; appears to be a local-dev hack

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change an existing migration (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which could destroy data if this migration is ever rerun (e.g., during certain reset/rebuild workflows or if the table exists unexpectedly). However, on a normal one-time migration run where the table does not yet exist, this does not introduce a runtime defect, so it’s more of a risky/undesirable change than a guaranteed bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key computed in poll_feed.rb is dead code, suggesting unimplemented feed-modification check causing full feed re-import every hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (building a Redis-style key based on `feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`, making it dead code in this diff. The job does fetch/parse the full feed every run (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `rss.items.each`), but it does not "fully re-import" in the sense of duplicating topics because `TopicEmbed.import` upserts by `embed_url` (unique index) and only revises when `content_sha1` changes. This is still a concrete, diff-grounded concern about an unimplemented feed-modification/conditional-fetch optimization, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor save changed to allow skip_validations at shared layer with no guard, letting any caller persist invalid posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, introducing a new capability for any caller of `revise!` to bypass model validations by passing `skip_validations: true`. The diff shows a new caller doing exactly that in `TopicEmbed.import` (`revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)`). This is a real, diff-grounded concern about expanding a shared-layer API in a way that can persist invalid posts if misused, but it’s not clearly a verifiable defect on its own (it may be intentional for imports and there’s no evidence user input can set this flag).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController hardcodes best posts count as literal 5 with no setting or constant, not configurable

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`, the embed endpoint hardcodes the number of "best" posts via `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. The diff shows no corresponding `SiteSetting`, constant, or parameter to configure this value, so the finding is accurate. This is not a correctness defect (it will work as-is), but it is a legitimate configurability/maintainability concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only edits to unrelated migration migrate_word_counts.rb add diff noise and conflict risk with no requirement traceability

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` shows only whitespace changes (removing trailing spaces on a blank line and adding a missing newline at EOF). While this does add minor diff noise, it’s a purely formatting/style nit and not a specific nontrivial review issue or defect introduced by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` invoked inline in `perform_retrieve` re-downloads and re-imports the entire RSS feed synchronously inside a background job with no timeout, just to find one embed_url, causing O(feed-size) work on every embed miss

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` (`perform_retrieve`), when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline and synchronously, then checks again for `TopicEmbed` existence. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item (`TopicEmbed.import(...)`). This is O(feed-size) work and re-downloads the whole feed on every embed miss; the diff also shows no explicit network timeouts around `open(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When `open(feed_polling_url)` fails, the exception kills the retrieve job because PollFeed is executed inline rather than enqueued, and RetrieveTopic's retry semantics don't cover the nested execution

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no rescue. If `open(...)` raises (network/timeout/invalid URL), the exception will bubble up and abort `perform_retrieve` before it can reach the `fetch_http` fallback, causing the `RetrieveTopic` execution path to fail for that embed request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The RSS lookup and HTTP-scrape path are parallel duplicated retrieval services for the 'find content for URL' concern

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two separate mechanisms to obtain content for an embed URL: (1) RSS/Atom polling via `Jobs::PollFeed` (which parses `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item), and (2) direct HTTP scraping via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (used by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`). `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` tries RSS first (by invoking `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), then falls back to HTTP scraping if the embed still doesn’t exist. This is not a correctness defect, but it does create parallel retrieval paths for the same “find/import content for URL” concern, which can be seen as an architectural duplication/scope concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` raises NoMethodError when `embed_by_username` is blank, since EmbedController#best only checks `embeddable_host`, causing crashed jobs and an infinite loading loop with no topic created

adjudication.rationale: `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` with no presence guard (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `EmbedController#best` only enforces `embeddable_host`/referer checks and enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` when no embed exists; it does not require `embed_by_username` to be set (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). If `embeddable_host` is configured but `embed_by_username` is blank/nil, the retrieve job will raise `NoMethodError` in `fetch_http`, preventing topic creation; the embed `loading` view auto-reloads every 30s, leading to an infinite loading loop (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in TopicEmbed: `where(embed_url: url).first` check followed later by `create!` lets two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs race, one crashing with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique instead of a rescue/re-find

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and, if blank, later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` with `embed_url: url`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so two concurrent callers (e.g., two `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` executions enqueued from `EmbedController#best`, or a retriever plus `PollFeed`) can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing one to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` with no rescue/retry/re-find shown in the diff. `TopicRetriever` also has a similar TOCTOU (`exists?` then later import), reinforcing the race window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in post.rb bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook)`, so plugin sanitizers/autolinkers/tracking silently never run on imported content

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an early return in `Post#cook`: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which means `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` is skipped for `:raw_html` posts. The new embed/RSS import path sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import`, so imported content will not run any `:after_post_cook` plugin hooks. This is a real, diff-grounded plugin/extensibility behavior change, but it appears intentional (comment + spec asserting `post.cooked == post.raw`), so it’s better classified as a non-bug concern about silently bypassing plugin processing on this new content type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import can be called from arbitrary paths (e.g. disqus.thor) with unrestricted raw HTML that skips the entire cooking pipeline, an evolvability/correctness boundary leak

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates/revises posts with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Callers like `Jobs::PollFeed` pass feed item content directly (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). The embed view then renders with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so untrusted feed HTML can be served verbatim, creating a concrete XSS/correctness boundary leak exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed update path assumes `embed.post` still exists; with no FK or dependent-destroy, a deleted topic leaves an orphaned TopicEmbed row that crashes on `revise!` with nil, permanently wedging that URL

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `post = embed.post` and unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` when content changes. The migration adds `topic_id`/`post_id` columns but no foreign keys, and the model has no `dependent:` behavior, so a deleted Post/Topic can leave an orphaned TopicEmbed row where `embed.post` is nil. That would raise when constructing/using PostRevisor, and because the existing TopicEmbed row remains, subsequent imports/retrievals will keep hitting the orphaned row (and TopicRetriever also bails early on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`), effectively wedging that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topic_id_for_embed` keeps returning a deleted topic id, so `TopicView.new(deleted_id)` runs on every page load of the embedding site

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is implemented as `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`, which does not verify the referenced `topics` row still exists (or isn’t deleted). Since `topic_embeds` has no FK/cascade or `dependent: :destroy` shown, a deleted/destroyed topic could leave a stale `topic_embeds` row, causing `EmbedController#best` to keep calling `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with an invalid/stale id instead of enqueuing retrieval/rendering loading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `feed_key` ("feed-modified:...") is computed but never used dead code; the conditional-fetch design is unimplemented and every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the full feed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (`"feed-modified:..."`) but never referenced anywhere in the job, so it is dead code in this diff. The job’s `execute` runs `poll_feed` hourly (when enabled) and `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key` or any conditional/cached fetch mechanism, meaning each run re-downloads and re-parses the full feed. This is a real, diff-grounded completeness/performance concern rather than a correctness break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sidekiq_options retry: false` on PollFeed means any transient network failure in the initial `open()` silently skips the whole hour's poll with no retry

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `Jobs::PollFeed` sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and performs network I/O via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. If `open(...)` raises due to a transient network error, Sidekiq will not retry this execution. That’s a real reliability/operability concern grounded in the diff, though it’s not strictly a correctness defect (the scheduled job will run again on the next hourly recurrence, and failures won’t be completely silent since Sidekiq will log the exception).

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query on `post.user` per rendered post in embed/best.html.erb loop, since TopicView is constructed with no user preload on a hot cached page; should use includes/batching

adjudication.rationale: The new view `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` does access `post.user` inside a loop, but the diff does not show how `@topic_view.posts` is loaded. `EmbedController#best` constructs `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`, and whether that preloads users (avoiding N+1) is determined by `TopicView` internals, which are not part of this diff. The claim that it is constructed "with no user preload" / causes N+1 on a cached page is therefore not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Origin check in embed.js uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of origin equality, so any string containing the site origin passes

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler checks `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is substring containment rather than an exact origin match. This can incorrectly accept messages from origins that are merely substrings/prefixes of `discourseUrl` (e.g., `discourseUrl` set to `https://discourse.example.com.evil.com/` would still accept `e.origin` of `https://discourse.example.com`). Proper origin validation should compare normalized origins for equality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `layouts/embed.html.erb` uses raw `request.referer` as postMessage targetOrigin inside a single-quoted string; a referer containing a quote breaks/escapes the script, and the write side and compare side disagree on canonical form

`content_sha1` is computed on pre-absolutization raw contents while the stored post contains absolutized URLs — no documented single source of truth for what it hashes, risking mismatches in future repair/reimport paths

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` is computed on the pre-absolutization `contents`, while the created/updated post stores `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (and updates via `revisor.revise!(..., absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)`). This is internally consistent for the current create/update flow (the sha is always recomputed from the same pre-absolutized input), so it’s not a verifiable defect. However, the finding is a real diff-grounded maintainability/consistency concern: the hash does not reflect the exact stored post content, and the code does not document that the “source of truth” for hashing is the un-absolutized feed/remote HTML, which could lead to mismatches if future code recomputes/repairs based on stored post raw/cooked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in an existing migration drops and recreates the table on re-run, destroying all TopTopic data — a data-loss change unrelated to this diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. `force: true` will drop an existing `top_topics` table before recreating it if the migration is ever re-executed (e.g., via `db:migrate:reset`, `db:setup` from migrations, or manual reruns), which could destroy data. However, this migration typically won’t rerun in normal `db:migrate` on an already-migrated production DB, so it’s a real review concern but not necessarily an immediate introduced runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task was silently rewritten: --category option removed and import switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote, losing category assignment for imported threads

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category` is removed and the code that derived `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)` is deleted. The import now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` do not accept or set any category in the shown diff. This is a clear behavioral regression: imported Disqus threads can no longer be assigned to a chosen category and will default elsewhere (likely uncategorized).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import now stores content as raw HTML (cook_method: raw_html) with no permalink markdown, an undocumented behavioral change

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Disqus import behavior in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`: it no longer creates the first post via `PostCreator` with `raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]"` and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches and parses remote HTML via `ruby-readability`, and `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking pipeline. Also, the previous explicit permalink markdown is indeed gone (replaced by an "Imported from" HTML snippet appended in `TopicEmbed.import`). Whether this is "undocumented" can’t be verified from the diff, but the behavioral change itself is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb modified to add force: true, which silently drops existing top_topics table and its data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` in `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` will drop an existing `top_topics` table before creating it, which would destroy any existing data if this migration is ever re-executed (e.g., during reset/re-run scenarios).

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook for raw_html posts returns raw directly, bypassing Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugin post-processing no longer applies to imported/embedded posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an early return in `Post#cook` for `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (`return raw ...`), which bypasses the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. The new embed/RSS import path sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`, so imported/embedded posts will indeed skip plugin post-processing. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change affecting plugin extensibility, but it appears intentional per the comment (“skip the rendering pipeline”), so it’s not necessarily a correctness bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported RSS/HTML content can carry unsanitized markup into cooked, rendered via raw post.cooked in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:18

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a raw-HTML rendering path for imported content: Post#cook returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), which disables escaping. For RSS polling, content is taken from `i.content` and only `CGI.unescapeHTML` is applied (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), with no sanitization shown in the diff. This means imported RSS/HTML can carry arbitrary markup into `post.cooked` and be rendered as-is, creating a verifiable XSS risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor change allows any caller of revise! to pass skip_validations: true, introducing a general-purpose validation bypass into the core editing path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and `revise!(user, new_raw, opts={})` accepts arbitrary `opts`. This does introduce a general-purpose validation bypass knob for any internal caller of `revise!` (and the new `TopicEmbed.import` path uses it). However, the diff alone doesn’t show an external/user-controlled path where an attacker can set `skip_validations: true`, so it’s a legitimate scope/architecture risk rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import stores remote content as raw_html posts, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and enabling stored XSS from embedded sites or RSS feeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook method and makes `Post#cook` return `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the embed view renders the cooked content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). For RSS polling, `PollFeed` passes feed `i.content` (only `unescapeHTML`/`scrub`) into `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This combination verifiably bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline for imported remote/feed HTML and then renders it as raw HTML, enabling stored XSS if the embedded site or feed content contains malicious markup/URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb interpolates the attacker-controlled Referer header unescaped into inline JavaScript postMessage call, enabling reflected XSS
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: the attacker-controlled Referer/request.referer header is interpolated into inline JavaScript without escaping, enabling XSS (e.g., via a postMessage call in embed.html.erb).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import interpolates the embed URL into raw HTML with single quotes, permitting HTML/script injection via crafted URLs

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the embed URL is interpolated directly into HTML without escaping: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or HTML characters in `url`. A crafted URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)`) would break out of the `href='...'` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML. This is especially exploitable because imported posts use `cook_method: :raw_html` (Post#cook returns `raw`) and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController relies solely on a client-forgeable Referer header check for access control on embed/best, allowing unauthenticated content reads

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated only by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then setting `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`. The `Referer` header is client-controlled/spoofable (and can be set by non-browser clients), so this is not a strong authorization mechanism for `/embed/best` content. The route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` has no auth requirement, so a caller can fetch embed content by providing a forged Referer matching the allowed host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js validates postMessage origins via substring containment instead of strict equality, allowing hostile frames with substring-matching origins to control iframe sizing

adjudication.rationale: In embed.js the origin check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which only accepts messages when `e.origin` is contained within `discourseUrl`. A “hostile frame with substring-matching origin” like `https://discourse.example.com.evil.com` would not be contained in `https://discourse.example.com/` and would be rejected. While strict equality would be cleaner, the specific claim that substring-matching hostile origins can control resizing is not supported by the logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb uses weak `response.should_not be_success` assertions that can't distinguish failure causes; three distinct tests assert the same thing and would pass regardless of which guard fires

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, multiple negative-path tests only assert `response.should_not be_success` (e.g., missing embed_url, missing host, and no referer). These assertions don’t verify which guard caused the failure or the expected status/exception, so the tests could still pass even if the controller fails for an unintended reason (or the wrong guard fires). This is a specific test-quality gap introduced with the new controller/spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever_spec.rb stubs out the behavior under test (`retrieved_recently?`), so the real Redis-throttle logic and perform_retrieve/fetch_http are never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`), and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked. This means the real Redis throttle path in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx/expire` logic) is never exercised, and neither are the downstream behaviors inside `perform_retrieve` (e.g., `fetch_http` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) in this spec. That’s a concrete test coverage gap created by the new throttling/retrieval logic, but not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb tests only the setting gates; the poll_feed import body (SimpleRSS.parse, url fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import) has zero assertions, and the new url fallback branch is untestable by existing tests

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, all examples exercise only Jobs::PollFeed#execute gating conditions and the delegation to poll_feed; there are no tests for Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed itself (which includes SimpleRSS.parse open(...), URL fallback to i.id when i.link is blank/non-http, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import calls). That leaves newly added nontrivial import logic unverified by the PR’s test additions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb update-path test only asserts a string appears; it doesn't verify PostRevisor#revise! invocation, content_sha1 update_column, or the content-unchanged no-revision short-circuit, and import_remote is unexercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial update logic in `TopicEmbed.import`: when an embed exists and `content_sha1` changes it calls `PostRevisor#revise!` and then `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)`, and when unchanged it should skip revision. In `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, the “Supports updating the post” example only asserts the resulting `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/` and does not exercise or assert the revision mechanics (e.g., that `PostRevisor#revise!` is invoked, `content_sha1` is updated, or that unchanged content short-circuits). Also, `import_remote` (newly added) is not covered by tests. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test/coverage concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb 'creates a topic view' test only verifies a mock call (returning nil) rather than the rendered response shape, and the loading/Jobs.enqueue branch's arguments are only covered indirectly

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the “creates a topic view when a topic_id is found” example only asserts `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` and does not validate the rendered template/body (response shape) for `/embed/best` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Also, the controller’s no-topic branch enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), but the spec doesn’t directly assert the enqueue call/arguments or the loading render, so that behavior isn’t explicitly covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method column default of 1 in migration is unverified against the Enum indexing, potentially reclassifying every existing post as raw_html and causing site-wide silent misrendering on next cook

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. Whether `default: 1` corresponds to `:regular` or `:raw_html` depends on how `Enum` indexes values, which is not shown in this diff. If the indexing were 0-based, `1` would map to `:raw_html` and `Post#cook` would start returning `raw` for existing posts (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), causing widespread misrendering; if 1-based, it’s fine. The finding is a valid diff-grounded risk but not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to already-shipped create_top_topics migration can drop existing top_topics table with all its data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. If this migration is ever re-run against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., in nonstandard restore/repair/partial-migrate scenarios), it can drop existing data, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CreateTopicEmbeds migration uses force: true unnecessarily, risking silent destruction of TopicEmbed rows if the migration is re-applied

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`. Using `force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, which could destroy existing `topic_embeds` data in atypical scenarios (e.g., migration re-run/redo, or if the table was created out-of-band). However, as a new migration creating a new table in the normal one-time migration path, it typically won’t cause data loss, so it’s more of a safety/maintainability concern than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_id/post_id in topic_embeds are plain integers with no foreign keys, leaving orphaned topic_embeds rows after topic/post deletion that crash EmbedController#best

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `t.integer :topic_id` / `:post_id` and adds only a unique index on `embed_url`, with no foreign keys or cascading deletes. Combined with `TopicEmbed` just using `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` (no `dependent:` behavior shown), deleting a Topic/Post could leave orphaned `topic_embeds` rows. The finding’s further claim that this will “crash `EmbedController#best`” is plausible (it blindly does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` from `pluck(:topic_id)`), but the diff doesn’t prove `TopicView.new` will raise on a missing topic, so the crash aspect isn’t strictly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unique index on embed_url prevents re-import of orphaned embeds because existing orphaned rows keep being found, passing nil to PostRevisor

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, an existing `topic_embeds` row is always reused (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`). If that row is orphaned (e.g., `post_id` points to a deleted post), then `post = embed.post` will be `nil`. On update, the code unconditionally does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` when `content_sha1` differs, which would pass `nil` to `PostRevisor` (likely raising). Separately, because the migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, the code cannot create a new `TopicEmbed` for the same URL to recover from an orphaned row. This defect is grounded in the diff (no orphan-handling logic is present).

adjudication_records.issue_text: update path via PostRevisor.revise! doesn't re-assert cook_method raw_html, so RSS HTML injected into existing posts goes through the normal markdown pipeline and gets mangled

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation path explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` via `PostCreator`, and that value is persisted on the post (`post.cook_method = ...` in `PostCreator#setup_post`). On the update path, `PostRevisor.revise!` is called on the existing `embed.post`; nothing in the diff shows `PostRevisor` resetting or overriding `cook_method`, so the post should retain `raw_html` and `Post#cook` will still return `raw` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Thus the claim that updates would go through the normal pipeline due to not “re-asserting” `cook_method` is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer change silently re-routes existing import behavior from Permalink raw post to TopicEmbed.import_remote, causing previously-imported threads to render differently after re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus Thor task from creating a topic with a simple raw permalink (PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](...)]" ...)) to calling TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]) (lib/tasks/disqus.thor). TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches and imports remote article HTML via ruby-readability and uses cook_method :raw_html, so the created first post’s content/rendering will differ from the previous importer behavior. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change in the import task (also removing the :category option), but the diff doesn’t prove it breaks runtime correctness—reruns already weren’t idempotent before—so it’s best classified as an important review concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:30 uses open-uri with no timeout and no size cap, allowing a slow/hung feed server to block the Sidekiq worker indefinitely, and this path is reachable from the request path via embed/best → retrieve_topic

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses open-uri without any explicit timeouts or response size limits, so a slow/hung feed server could block the Sidekiq worker thread. This code is also invoked from request-triggered flow: EmbedController#best enqueues `retrieve_topic`, which calls TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve; when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` it runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, reaching the open-uri call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:52 import_remote reads open(url) with no timeout or content-length cap, potentially reading a huge response fully into memory from a URL only regex-checked as ^https?://

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` `import_remote` does `open(url).read` before any scheme/size validation and without any timeout or response-size cap. The only regex check (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) is in `import`, but it happens *after* the full remote body is read. This can lead to unbounded memory/time consumption (DoS) when fetching a very large/slow URL, and the issue is directly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb: with sidekiq_options retry: false, the first item that raises (e.g. nil.scrub NoMethodError when i.content is nil on an Atom feed) aborts the loop, silently dropping all remaining items with no retry

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false` and processes items via `rss.items.each`. Inside the loop it unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` (possible for some feed items depending on RSS/Atom fields), this will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the entire job mid-loop, leaving remaining items unprocessed. With retries disabled, Sidekiq will not rerun the job to recover.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:20-22: content_sha1 is updated via update_column even if the underlying revisor.revise!/post save failed, so future polls see 'no change' and the dropped revision is never retried

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when content_sha1 differs it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. The diff also changes PostRevisor to do `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and `TopicEmbed` passes `skip_validations: true`, meaning the save can still fail due to callbacks/DB errors even without validations. If `revise!`/the save returns false (no exception), the SHA1 would still be updated, causing later polls to think the content is up-to-date even though the post wasn’t revised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb/retrieve_topic.rb: retrieval failure is invisible to the user — loading page reloads every 30s indefinitely; failures are silent (fetch_http returns on username mismatch, import_remote returns nil on 404) and the throttle key is committed before retrieval, blocking retries for 60s

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed flow where, if no TopicEmbed exists, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading` (which unconditionally reloads every 30s). In `TopicRetriever`, failures can result in no embed ever being created without any user-visible error: `fetch_http` silently returns when `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` is blank, and `perform_retrieve` can also bail out without creating an embed (e.g., host mismatch via `invalid_host?`). Additionally, `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key (`setnx` + `expire`) before attempting `perform_retrieve`, so a failed/short-circuited retrieval still blocks retries for 60s, exacerbating the loading loop. (Note: the finding’s claim that `import_remote` returns nil on 404 isn’t shown; `open(url)` would typically raise.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:24-26: update branch crashes with NoMethodError when embed.post is nil (deleted post, no FK cascade); also create branch returns a possibly-invalid failed post as if import succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the SHA changed. Since the migration adds no foreign key constraint (only `post_id null: false`) and posts can be deleted without a cascade, `embed.post` can be `nil`, causing a NoMethodError/exception when revising. This is a real edge-case crash exposed by the diff. The second claim (returning an invalid/failed post as success) is less directly verifiable from the diff because it depends on PostCreator#create semantics, but the nil-post crash in the update branch is grounded here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:36-37: malformed/non-http feed items are silently dropped with no logging, and with retry:false they are permanently dropped until the feed changes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each RSS item’s URL is taken from `i.link`, falling back to `i.id` if `link` is blank or non-http (lines shown around the `url = i.id if ...` logic). The job then calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` immediately `return`s unless the URL matches `^https?://`, with no logging. So malformed/non-http items will be silently skipped every run. However, this is not a hard defect (the job keeps running and will keep re-attempting on subsequent schedules); it’s primarily an observability/edge-case handling concern rather than a verifiable broken behavior.
